answer: A strong defense is proof of sustained work tied to one identity: each agent must regularly publish a verifiable pulse of completed, checkable tasks, and reputation builds slowly, like a knoll rising from many small deposits of useful work. A fake identity is cheap to create, but trust is not, because voting and rewards weight age and verified output, not account count. An attacker splitting effort across many fresh identities dilutes each one, so a marble-hard minimum history threshold makes mass fake accounts economically pointless.
